Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module four on electrochemical equilibria and in today's class we are going to discuss about the different types of electrodes.

Key details

  • The metal ion electrode, the metal insoluble salt ion electrode, the gas electrode, amalgam electrode, redox electrode and iron selective electrode.
  • In order to form a cell, we need two half cells, and therefore two electrodes are required.
  • The first one is a metal ion electrode.
  • We have a metal rod which is in contact with a solution of its own ions.
  • Remember that we always write the reduction reaction because we all talk about reduction potentials.
  • Since a potential is formed at the.
  • Electrode and the solution interface.
  • This is a familiar Nant equation which we have already learnt.
  • M of MN plus is equal to E naught that is the standard electrode potential of M Mn plus two point three zero three R T over NF log of Mn plus.
  • So that is the first type of electrode.
  • How would we describe this electrode?
  • As the name suggests, we have a metal which is in contact with a sparingly soluble salt of the metal and that is again dipped in a solution of soluble salt of the same anion.
  • Mercury, which is a metal, and that is in contact with a sparingly soluble salt of mercury, that is.
  • A G2 Cl2 and now this is dipped in a solution of KCl.
  • Because it should be the solution of a soluble salt of the same anion.
  • And here what do we have in silver chloride electrode?
  • We have the silver metal which is in contact with silver chloride and that is in contact with HCl.
  • The equation is AG Cl plus electron is giving you AG plus Cl minus.
  • What we have to be careful about is that this is not A G plus and even if we write A G plus the equation would not be balanced.
  • Plus Cl minus and we can see this electrode over here in the diagram we have a silver wire which is coated with silver chloride that is the sparingly soluble salt of silver and that is dipped in a solution either of KCl or SCl.
  • It should contain it should be a solution containing the anion and the anion of the salt is Cl minus.
